proposals.edit: jaw -> long_slide (sector_radius_mm=50)
proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face (8 tasks) and squeezed_down_out (gelatin). Every failing object is wide and low (73–96 mm across, only 30–58 mm tall). The stock jaw swings on an 81 mm radius, so at these openings its fingertip has risen +17 to +27 mm above the fixed one. That is at or above each object's top: the tops sit +15 to +29 mm above centre, and the logs show tuna +27 tip vs top +17, sugar +23 vs +23, pudding +17–19 vs +19. The face is also tilted 33–53 deg. So the moving jaw lands on the top face and pushes 66–84 deg downward, or (gelatin) touches the side 33 deg off horizontal and pushes the box down and out.
proposals.principle: A fingertip on a swinging joint rises by about R(1−cos q), and its face is parallel to the fixed face at only one opening. A finger holds a side only if, at that object's opening, it reaches below the top, and only horizontal antipodal contacts hold without squeezing the object out. A slide keeps the finger's height and angle the same at every opening.
proposals.hypothesis: Brief numbers for long_slide at sector_radius_mm=50: fingertips up to 103 mm apart, and at 35, 55 and 85 mm the face is 0 deg, the tip is +1 mm, and the squeeze is 32 N. The widest failing object is the 96 mm mustard bottle, which needs about 100 mm with clearance, so 50 mm is the only end of the range that reaches it (30 mm gives only 68 mm). With the tip at +1 mm, it sits well under every failing object's top (+15 to +29 mm), and the contact is horizontal. Holding force: 2·0.5·32 = 32 N against 5.0 N for the 514 g sugar box, and 2·0.4·32 = 26 N against 4.2 N for the mustard. Arm load for the sugar box: 0.41 + 0.77 = 1.18 N·m plus a few tens of grams for the slide, under the 1.62 N·m stall, so no 12 V servos are needed (we couldn't afford them anyway: $68 vs $40). Why cheaper moves fail: no value of the current jaw or of pads fixes this. Pads at 45 deg still leave the tip at +14 mm and the face at +14 deg at 85 mm, and wider at 92–96 mm. The parallelogram still rises (+33 mm at 85 mm for link 90), and the prismatic jaw tops out at 68 mm. Cost: $6.40 (2 lm3uu, 2 steel_rod_3x150), 3 days, 216 machine minutes, all within budget.
risks: Rolling round objects (golf_ball, apple, lemon, plum, tennis_ball, racquetball, strawberry, tomato_soup_can): today's tilted face was part of their tuned grasp. Expected to survive: a vertical face touches a sphere or cylinder exactly at its equator, the case the principles name as neutral, and 32 N is more squeeze than the 20 N they hold with now.

Small objects (dice 17 mm, large_marker 19 mm, wood_block_cube 26 mm): the slide's travel is 50 mm/rad over 1.92 rad = 96 mm, so the minimum opening is about 7 mm. They stay reachable with a flat face and +1 mm tip.
cup (13 g) and foam_brick: squeeze rises to 32 N; System 1 can lower the close target if needed.
The jaw closes faster per radian (50 mm/rad); System 1 retunes close speed.

iterations.notes:
I sent two proposals. The main one swaps the jaw for the long slide. The cheap one adds pads to the current jaw.

**Diagnosis.** All five failing groups (gelatin, pudding, sugar, mustard, tuna) are wide (73–96 mm across) and low (30–58 mm tall). The current hinged jaw swings on an 81 mm radius, so at those openings its fingertip rises 17–27 mm above the fixed one. That puts it level with or above the object's top, so it presses on the top face instead of the side (or, on the gelatin box, squeezes it down and out). This is the jaw's geometry, and System 1 can't tune it away.

**1. Swap the jaw for `long_slide` at sector radius 50 mm.** This is the only part in the catalogue that both stays flat and level and opens wide enough for the 96 mm mustard bottle.
- **What the brief shows:** the face stays at 0 degrees and the tip at +1 mm at every opening, with 32 N of squeeze and up to 103 mm between fingertips.
- **Arm:** the 514 g sugar box needs about 1.18 N·m at the shoulder, under the 1.62 N·m stall, so no 12 V servos are needed (they'd cost $68 against the $40 left anyway).
- **What I'd buy:** 2 × lm3uu_bearing and 2 × steel_rod_3x150, for $6.40 with a 3-day lead time, plus 216 machine minutes.
- **Risks to held groups:** round objects should still hold, because a vertical face touches them at the middle of their height. Small objects stay reachable, since the jaw closes to about 7 mm.
- **I expect it to gain all five groups.**

**2. Add pads to the current jaw (no swap).** This costs nothing and takes 16 machine minutes.
- **Settings:** pads tilted back 30 degrees with a 2 mm TPU skin (friction 0.9), no extension, groove or lip.
- **Expected gains:** gelatin, tuna and possibly pudding. Sugar and mustard probably still miss.
- **Main risk:** the tilt leans the jaw face the other way on dice, the marker and the wood cube, and the moving fingertip ends up lower than the fixed one.

The two proposals change different slots, so if both are kept they'll also be tried together. Together they cost $6.40 and 232 machine minutes, within the budget.

idea.description: A long_slide at sector 49 mm, below the radius whose sector hit the wrist. A printed spacer moves the fixed jaw outward 10 mm, so the slide travels 82-102 mm instead of 72-92 mm. The three failing groups (pudding_box, sugar_box, mustard_bottle) all fail the same way. The hinged moving jaw is near the end of its swing, its tip has risen 19 to 20 mm above the fixed tip, and its pad lands on the object's top.

**What the record rules out**
- **Pad angle:** both earlier angle-only pad moves were tried. 30→38 deg gained gelatin and tuna, and 45 deg lost banana. The angle can't do more.
- **Long slide:** it was tried 8 times. It hit the wrist at sector 50 and was refused. At 46 to 49 its rack pressed on the top of the lying tomato soup can, even with 8 and 20 mm reach. I won't repeat it.
- **Parallelogram:** the tip still swings on a circle of radius 50 to 90 mm, so the brief shows it rising +49 mm at 85 mm. Worse than now.
- **Prismatic:** opens only to 59 mm, too narrow.
- **12 V servos:** they cost $68 and we have $40, and they aren't needed. Sugar needs 1.18 N*m against a 1.62 N*m stall. Its stall came from pressing on the box top.

**What hasn't been tried**
Pad reach on the stock hinged jaw. The tip rises by about R(1 - cos q). A longer finger reaches the same opening at a smaller angle, so the tip rises less and the face tilts less. It also opens wider at full swing, which the 96 mm mustard bottle needs.

**The two proposals**
Both are $0, use only parts on hand, and have no lead time. They bracket the reach at 18 mm and 30 mm. The main risks are the narrowest objects (dice, marker), where longer pads tilted inward could meet before they close on the object. There is also a squeeze drop of about 20%, which still leaves about 2.5 to 3x the margin for the heavy metal cans.

**The new part: a rise-compensating moving pad**
The moving pad rides on a printed PLA dovetail running down the moving jaw's face. A printed link connects the pad, through an MR63 pivot, to a second MR63 pivot on the gripper body, about 25 mm from the jaw hinge. The link is slotted at its body end.
- Below 0.64 rad (55 mm opening) the slot is slack and the pad rests on a hard stop in today's position. Every object narrower than 55 mm sees the current geometry unchanged: dice, marker, wood cube, screwdriver, golf ball, strawberry, foam brick, plum.
- Above 0.64 rad the link goes taut. It pulls the pad down the jaw by about the hinge's rise, about 20 mm at 1.07 rad. That holds the moving tip near −3 to +2 mm of the fixed tip from 55 to about 100 mm.
- The link is a two-force member, so the pad's height is set by the linkage, not by friction in the dovetail. The vertical load on it is at most about 2.2 N per side, from mustard.
- Moving the pad 20 mm further from the hinge also widens the swing by about 20 × sin 1.2 ≈ 19 mm. The maximum opening becomes about 110 mm, which clears mustard's 96 mm.
- Squeeze falls to about 1.62 N·m / 0.10 m ≈ 16 N. Mustard needs about 7 N (431 g, μ 0.4, ×1.3 margin for the lift's acceleration). Pudding needs about 2 N.
- The face tilt remains, about 19° bottom-out at 90 mm. tan 19° = 0.34 is below cardboard's 0.5, and marginal against mustard's 0.4. The self-aligning pivot pad recorded in iteration 5 would remove that tilt, and the two parts fit together.

I'm proposing one change, and it's an untested idea (the third on record), because no move in the catalogue can fix this failure.

**What fails:** on both pudding_box and mustard_bottle the moving fingertip has risen too far by the time the jaw is wide open, so it lands on the object's top instead of its side.

**What I propose:** a rise-compensating moving pad that slides down the moving jaw, pulled by a slotted link. It stays where it is today below 55 mm, so the small-object groups keep today's geometry. Above that it cancels most of the fingertip's rise and should widen the opening to about 110 mm. Parts to buy: 2 MR63 bearings ($1.80, 3 days lead). **Main risk:** banana. A lower moving pad has twice tripped the force limit on it. The groups between 55 and 85 mm will also need System 1 to raise its grasp depth so the lowered tip clears the table.

It would fit with the iteration-5 self-aligning pivot pad: this part removes the rise, that one removes the face tilt.

idea.name: parallel-link moving pad (pad-level four-bar on the stock revolute jaw)
idea.description: A printed pad carrier pivots on an MR63 bearing 15 mm above the moving jaw's fingertip. A 15 mm crank on the carrier connects through a 66 mm printed link to a ground pivot on the gripper body, which also runs on an MR63. That ground pivot sits 15 mm from the hinge axis, offset the same way as the crank. Hinge, pad pivot, crank pin and ground pivot form a parallelogram, so the pad keeps its body-frame orientation (face vertical, parallel to the fixed jaw) while the jaw swings from -0.17 to 1.20 rad. The fingertip still follows the 81 mm hinge circle, so the existing grasp-depth tuning handles the rise. The link runs outboard of the 10 mm pad width so it stays clear of the object. The fixed jaw keeps its current PLA pad.

iterations.notes:
The mustard bottle can't be fixed with the parts in the catalogue, so I'm proposing a new part, a pad held vertical by a small link. The simulator can't build new parts, so this gets recorded and costed but not tested this round.

Why no catalogue move works for the mustard bottle (96 mm across):
- **Pad settings on the current jaw are used up.** Every value that matters has been tried: pad angle 30/38/42/44/45, reach 4/18/30, TPU 2 down to 0. Angles above 42 lost the banana, and even 45 leaves the moving face 22 deg off parallel at 96 mm. A face parallel at 96 mm would need about 66 deg, beyond the pad's 45 deg limit. A lip narrows the opening below 96 mm, and the groove and width settings act across the pad, not up it.
- **The long slide can't open far enough.** At sector 49 it opens about 96 mm, which leaves no clearance for a 96 mm bottle. Sector 50 is refused for parts colliding, and the slide already lost tomato_soup_can and potted_meat_can when its rack pressed on their tops.
- **The other jaws are worse.** The parallelogram jaw's fingertip rises +42 mm at 85 mm, worse than the current +13. The prismatic jaw opens only 63 mm.
- **The 12 V servos are out.** They cost $68 against $40 left, and arm torque isn't the problem: the shoulder needs 1.06 N*m against a 1.62 stall.

**What's actually failing:** at 96 mm the moving face leans in 23 deg and its fingertip sits 23 mm above the fixed one. The top of the pad lands on the bottle's rounded shoulder and pushes it down at 61 deg instead of squeezing it sideways.

**The proposed fix** keeps the stock jaw, which holds all 20 passing objects, and adds a pad that a short link holds vertical at every opening. The fingertip still rises, but the grasp depth can be tuned to put it at the bottle's middle. A vertical face there pushes almost horizontally, so the two jaws squeeze straight across and friction can hold the 431 g bottle.

**What it would take:**
- **To buy:** 2 × MR63 bearings ($0.90 each, $1.80 total, 3 days lead time).
- **From what's on hand:** 3 M3 screws, 4 M2 screws, and about 8 g of PLA (about 40 machine minutes).

That is well within the $40, 7 days and 580 machine minutes left.

**Risks to objects that pass now:** sugar_box and pudding_box need the full opening, and the round fruits and balls currently rely on the tuned tilted face. If the balls slip on a vertical face, the existing groove setting would centre them.

idea.name: re-centred moving-jaw hinge (servo axis moved ~22 mm outward, jaw re-clocked 0.3 rad)
idea.description: This replaces the stock static gripper frame and moving jaw with printed versions, and keeps the same STS3215 jaw servo and the same 81 mm hinge-to-tip radius. The frame relocates the jaw servo's axis about 22 mm away from the fixed jaw, at the same height as now. The new moving jaw places its fingertip 0.3 rad further toward the closing direction about the axis, so it still meets the fixed jaw at q≈0 within the -0.17..1.20 rad range. The tip's arc is then centred on the servo range: its lowest point is at about q=0.55 (about 55 mm opening) instead of q=0.25. Results by the model: maximum opening about 105 mm (stock 99); moving-tip rise vs fixed about +2 mm at 17 mm, -10 mm at mid, +5 mm at 96 mm (stock -9, ..., +23); squeeze unchanged at 20 N. The pads part (design/fingers.py) carries over, but its pad_angle must be re-fitted so the face is parallel at about q=0.8.
idea.test: Give the simulator's revolute jaw builder two new parameters: hinge_offset_mm (the servo axis moved along the closing axis, 0-30 mm, with the axis height held) and clock_rad (the jaw's hinge-to-tip direction rotated 0-0.4 rad, with the closed position kept near q=0). Then run the brief's opening/face/tip table and the full task set at hinge_offset 22 mm, clock 0.3 rad, letting System 1 re-fit pad_angle_deg near 25-35 deg.
